newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Optus no comment on CEO resign report.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Optus no comment on CEO resign report.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said it had no comment on a report in the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper that the company's chief executive, Ziggy Switkowski, did not have the support of the board of directors and was about to resign.
"The company is making no comment at all. It would be completely inappropriate," an Optus spokeswoman said.

The newspaper said Switkowski's resignation could be announced as soon as Friday and the departure was based on boardroom concern about his handling of strategic issues such as the loss-making investment in pay television.
It also said the departure of Switkowski would almost certainly delay the float of Optus Communications, the second largest telecoms group in Australia, to calendar 1998.
Optus had hoped to float this year before one-third of the state-owned Telstra Corp hit the market, raising more than A$8 billion.
Switkowski joined Optus about a year ago after a long career with Kodak.
Optus has three key shareholders, local transport and health care group Mayne Nickless Ltd with 24.9 percent, and equal 24.5 percent shareholders BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc.
The newspaper said Switkowski could be replaced by Rod Olsen, the deputy chief executive of Cable and Wireless who is in charge of international operations.
